newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares ease, seen flat or down this week.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares ease, seen flat or down this week.

text.p: Polish shares eased from a 35-month high in surging turnover on Wednesday and analysts saw a flat market or falls in profit-taking for the rest of the week after the bourse's 38-percent gain since mid-December.
The main market's WIG index eased 0.2 percent to 18,295.0 points and turnover rose 45 percent to 337.7 million zlotys ($112.6) on both markets as 42 issues fell, 32 rose and 14 were flat.
Analysts said worse-than-expected January company earnings reports released on Tuesday might additionally be cooling down the investor mood.

"One could have expected that companies would show better earnings than in November and December, but besides construction firms, no sectors showed shining results (on Tuesday)," said Pawel Hominski of Magnus brokerage.

Analysts said computer maker Optimus SA plunged the daily maximum 10 percent in heavy trade after the company on Tuesday denied a market rumour that Microsoft had bought most of its convertible bonds.

They said garment maker Prochnik SA, construction firm Elektromontaz Export SA and industrial boilermaker Rafako SA fell after showing January net losses on Tuesday, but could not explain construction firm Mostostal Krakow's 10-percent surge.
In continuous trade the WIG 20 index stayed virtually flat at 1,880.1 points.
